images.prompt: A scatter plot with several data points and a single regression line. For each data point, a vertical line segment connects the point to the regression line. At the end of each vertical segment, a small square is drawn, representing the squared residual for that point. The pedagogical intent is to visually explain that OLS minimizes the sum of the areas of these squares.

images.prompt: A 2x2 grid of residual plots. Plot 1 (Top-Left, "Good"): A scatter plot of residuals on the y-axis vs. predicted values on the x-axis. Points are randomly scattered around the horizontal line at y=0, forming a roughly rectangular cloud. Plot 2 (Top-Right, "Bad - Non-linearity"): A scatter plot of residuals vs. predicted values showing a clear U-shaped pattern, indicating that a linear model is not appropriate. Plot 3 (Bottom-Left, "Bad - Heteroscedasticity"): A scatter plot of residuals vs. predicted values showing a funnel shape, where the spread of residuals increases as predicted values increase. Plot 4 (Bottom-Right, "Bad - Outliers/Influential Points"): A scatter plot of residuals vs. predicted values with a few points far away from the main cloud, indicating potential outliers.
